title: Article Eater Bridge Warrant
description: Explicit assumption licensing transfer of knowledge between domains. Bridge warrants are load-bearing epistemic structures that determine whether evidence transfers across domains (Cartwright & Hardie, 2012).

bridge_id.description: Unique identifier for this bridge warrant

target_domain.description: Domain to which evidence is transferred (e.g., 'architectural_perception', 'environmental_psychology')

bridge_type.description: Type of bridging assumption: mechanism (same causal pathway), functional (same outcome, different mechanisms), analogical (structural similarity), constitutive (target contains source)

warrant_statement.description: Natural language statement of the bridging assumption

assumed_mechanism.description: For mechanism bridges: the conserved causal pathway (e.g., 'amygdala threat detection')

confidence.description: Probability that the bridge holds (0-1). Defaults: constitutive=0.85, mechanism=0.60, functional=0.50, analogical=0.35

status.description: Current epistemic status of the bridge. Lifecycle: hypothesized -> supported/contested -> failed -> revised

source_beliefs.description: Belief IDs from source domain that ground this bridge

target_beliefs.description: Belief IDs in target domain that this bridge supports

evidence_for.description: Belief IDs or paper IDs supporting the bridge

evidence_against.description: Belief IDs or paper IDs disconfirming the bridge

failure_record.description: Record of bridge failure, if applicable

failed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when failure was recorded

disconfirming_evidence.description: Belief IDs of evidence that disconfirmed the bridge

suggested_revision.description: Suggested downgrade to a different bridge type that might still hold

provenance.description: Tracking information for the bridge warrant

last_updated.description: When the bridge was last modified

voi_flag.description: Value of Information flag - true if this bridge is a high-value target for investigation

bridged_credence_cache.description: Cached result of compute_bridged_credence() for lazy evaluation
